about.title: Tehachapi Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Tehachapi's mix of small-town streets and busy stretches like E Tehachapi Boulevard and Valley Boulevard sees a steady flow of traffic, and public crash records show 24 injury collisions and 35 injured people in the most recent year on file, with Tuesday afternoons between 2 and 4 p.m. showing more reported crashes than other times. Behind each number is someone dealing with pain, missed work, and a pile of paperwork from an insurance company that isn't on their side. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney familiar with Kern County roads and courts. The attorney you're matched with works on contingency, meaning there's no upfront cost and no fee unless your case results in a recovery. Our goal is simple: help you find someone who can explain your options clearly, so you're not navigating this alone while trying to heal.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file suit in California, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Waiting to see how you feel could cost you the ability to file at all.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce What You Recover
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, so even if you're found partly responsible, you can still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help make sure fault isn't unfairly pinned on you before you say something on record that hurts your claim.

items.title: Recorded Statements Rarely Help the Injured Person
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement early, before you know the full extent of your injuries. An independent attorney can advise you on what to say — and what to hold off on — while evidence like scene photos and witness accounts is still preserved.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in Tehachapi?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. That timeline can be much shorter, sometimes six months, if a government entity like a city or county was involved. Because deadlines vary by circumstance, it's worth having an attorney review your situation early.

items.question: What if the accident happened on a Kern County road and I was partly at fault?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame for the crash. Your recovery is typically reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated entirely. An independent attorney can help gather evidence to fairly represent what happened.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally wise to speak with an attorney before giving any recorded statement, since insurers sometimes use early statements to minimize claims. You're not required to give one right away. LawProactive can connect you with someone who can walk through what to expect.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if your case results in a recovery. There's no upfront cost to find out if you have a claim.
